creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From the tooling feedback hub (a_2x3D6uh63), Muster 0.24.0, four sightings 2026-11-09 to 11-10. An integrator on a devenv (wren) and a worker on the Mac (bison) talk in group bison+wren.

When bison blocked at a dialog, the Mac's daemon posted its @muster notice in a new group, `bison+wren@mac` (or, seen from the other side, `bison+wren@devenv`), rather than the existing one, and late: the dialog had been answered before the notice arrived. From then on a plain `muster msg post --to bison` (or the worker's `--to wren`) is refused: "this post could go to bison+wren or bison+wren@mac; say which with --group". Workers following the parallel-work skill ("a post finds it without --group") hit this after any blocked dialog, and later idle notices keep landing in the second group, so one conversation is split in two.

Wanted: put a linked machine's @muster notices about a pane in the existing group for that pair; and drop a blocked notice whose dialog was answered before it was delivered (a-stall-notice is the same check for stall notices).
title: A linked machine's @muster notice opens a second group for a pair, and every later post needs --group
